title: Equivalent fractions on fraction bars
examples: How do I find equivalent fractions?

explain.say: Would you rather have half a chapati or 2 quarters of it? Trick question! Look at the two bars: the top one shows one half, and the bottom one shows 2 quarters. The shaded parts are exactly as long.

Fractions that show the same amount are called equivalent fractions. Equivalent means worth the same. One half and 2 quarters match, even though the bottom bar has more, smaller pieces. Can you see the shaded parts line up?
Now the bottom bar has 6 equal parts, called sixths, and 3 are shaded. 3 sixths also line up with one half! What do you notice about 3 and 6?

It works for thirds too. One third lines up with 2 sixths. The trick: multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. 1 times 2 is 2, and 3 times 2 is 6. Can you find another fraction equal to one third?

You have cracked it! Three quarters equals 6 eighths. Doubling the top and bottom just cuts every piece in two. Wow: a fraction wall shows all of these at once. Challenge: what fraction with 10 at the bottom equals one half?

faq.a: Equivalent fractions show the same amount with different numbers. One half, 2 quarters and 3 sixths are all equivalent.
Yes. Cut a bar into 4 equal parts and shade 2, and you have shaded exactly half of it. So 2 quarters equals one half.
asks: Are 2 quarters equal to a half?

faq.q: How do I find equivalent fractions?
faq.a: Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. One half with both numbers doubled gives 2 quarters; with both tripled, it gives 3 sixths.
asks: How do I make an equal fraction?

faq.q: Why do the top and bottom both change?
faq.a: When you cut every piece into 2, there are twice as many pieces in the whole and twice as many shaded. So the amount stays the same.
asks: Why multiply the top and the bottom?

faq.a: A fraction wall is a stack of bars, each cut into a different number of equal parts. Shaded parts that line up are equivalent.
asks: How does a fraction wall work?

facts: Multiplying the top and bottom of a fraction by the same number gives an equivalent fraction.

quiz.say: Which fraction is equivalent to 1 over 2?
quiz.why: 4 out of 8 equal parts is exactly half.

wrong.0: 1/4 is half of a half, so it is smaller.

quiz.say: One third equals how many sixths?
quiz.why: 3 times 2 is 6, so the top must be 1 times 2, which is 2.

wrong.1: 3/6 is one half, which is bigger than 1/3.
